quiz.title: Class 12 Integration Miscellaneous Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight mixed questions covering partial fractions, integration by parts, substitution, special forms and definite integrals. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Put u = x², so du = 2x dx. The integral becomes ∫ cos u du = sin u + C = sin(x²) + C.

questions.q: By partial fractions, 1/[(x−1)(x+1)] can be written as:
questions.explanation: Set 1/[(x−1)(x+1)] = A/(x−1) + B/(x+1). Solving gives A = ½ and B = −½, so the answer is ½[1/(x−1) − 1/(x+1)].

questions.q: Using integration by parts, ∫ x eₓ dx equals:
questions.explanation: Take u = x, dv = eₓ dx. Then ∫ x eₓ dx = x eₓ − ∫ eₓ dx = x eₓ − eₓ + C = eₓ(x − 1) + C.

questions.q: The value of the definite integral ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2x dx is:
questions.explanation: ∫ 2x dx = x². Evaluating from 0 to 1 gives 1² − 0² = 1.

questions.q: For the special form ∫ dx/(x² + a²), the result is:
questions.explanation: This is the standard form ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) + C.
Let u = ln x, so du = (1/x) dx. The integral becomes ∫ u du = u²/2 + C = ½(ln x)² + C.

questions.q: Using the property of definite integrals, ∫ from −a to a of an odd function f(x) dx equals:
options: 2 ∫ from 0 to a of f(x) dx
∫ from 0 to a of f(x) dx
questions.explanation: For an odd function f(−x) = −f(x), the symmetric integral ∫ from −a to a f(x) dx = 0.

questions.q: The special form ∫ dx/(x² − a²) equals:
questions.explanation: The standard result is ∫ dx/(x² − a²) = (1/2a) ln|(x − a)/(x + a)| + C.

faq.q: How do I decide which integration method to use in this exercise?
faq.a: Look at the form of the integrand first. A product of two different functions usually calls for integration by parts, a rational function with factorable denominator suggests partial fractions, and anything where an inner function's derivative is present points to substitution. Special forms like 1/(x²+a²) are worth memorising outright.

faq.q: What order should I try methods in if I am stuck?
faq.a: Start with substitution, since it is fastest when it works. If the integrand is a ratio of polynomials, check whether the degree of the numerator is less than the denominator and then split into partial fractions. Save integration by parts for products like x eₓ or x sin x.

faq.q: Why do definite integrals sometimes come out to zero here?
faq.a: When the limits are symmetric, from −a to a, and the integrand is an odd function, the areas above and below the axis cancel exactly, giving zero. Spotting odd or even symmetry before integrating can save a lot of work.

faq.q: Do I need to memorise the standard integral forms?
faq.a: Yes. The forms for 1/(x²+a²), 1/(x²−a²), 1/√(a²−x²) and their relatives appear across the miscellaneous exercise and in board exams. Knowing them on sight turns hard-looking problems into one-line answers.
